problems.name: B-meson CP asymmetries
problems.description: Fit the source-era discrepancy in neutral B-meson CP observables with an explicit parameter region or benchmark satisfying the source's stated constraints. This is a historical target, not a claim that the discrepancy persists today.

problems.name: Baryon asymmetry
problems.description: Generate the observed cosmic baryon asymmetry through a quantitatively evaluated mechanism, with its thermal history, CP sources and parameter assumptions stated.

problems.name: Bottom forward–backward asymmetry
problems.description: Fit the LEP-era bottom-quark forward–backward asymmetry discrepancy while respecting the other constraints examined in the cited analysis. This is a historical, source-specific experimental target, not a claim of a current anomaly.

problems.name: Charged-fermion flavour
problems.description: Reproduce charged-fermion mass hierarchies and mixing patterns to the accuracy explicitly demonstrated by the source. Order-of-magnitude textures and precision fits must be distinguished; suppression of flavour-changing processes alone does not qualify.

problems.name: Cosmic inflation
problems.description: Calculate an inflationary regime with primordial perturbations compatible with the data examined in the source, stating the field trajectory, couplings and relevant reheating assumptions.

problems.name: Dark matter
problems.description: Reproduce the cosmological dark-matter abundance with sufficiently stable states, under the production history and constraints examined in the source. A candidate without an abundance calculation does not qualify.

problems.name: Electroweak hierarchy
problems.description: Demonstrate radiative protection of the weak scale or a calculated separation of scales over a stated energy range. The cutoff, symmetry assumptions and residual tuning must be identified; limited-cutoff protection is not a complete Planck-scale solution.

problems.name: Gauge-coupling unification
problems.description: Calculate a common high-scale value for the three measured SM gauge couplings, with the spectrum, thresholds and approximation stated. This target alone does not establish realistic fermion masses or a complete viable grand-unified theory.

problems.name: Neutrino masses
problems.description: Construct a neutrino mass spectrum compatible with measured oscillation scales. A mass-generating mechanism or a sub-eV scale estimate alone does not qualify; the demonstrated spectrum and any mixing assumptions must be stated.

problems.name: Strong CP
problems.description: Demonstrate suppression of the effective QCD CP angle, for example through the computed axion-potential minimum, under explicit symmetry and breaking assumptions.

entry_problems.result: For the unbroken complex-singlet portal with no additional interactions, the two degenerate real components double the calculated relic density at fixed mass and coupling. The paper analytically obtains the full-abundance contour by raising log10(lambda_hS) by approximately 0.15 and correspondingly rescales direct-detection contours. This supplies source-era thermal-relic solutions for this specified degenerate complex model.

With PQ breaking before inflation and no subsequent restoration, the calculated misalignment relation and reviewed global fit admit DFSZ axions supplying all dark matter for mass 0.12 micro-eV to 0.15 meV, conditional on the initial-angle prior and stated cosmology.

The DFSZ anomaly yields the axion-gluon coupling, and the calculated QCD axion potential has its CP-conserving absolute minimum at zero effective theta, assuming the PQ symmetry is not spoiled by additional explicit breaking.

locators: Sec. II.3, minimal fraternal particle content
Secs. III.1–III.4, Eqs. (11)–(26), particularly Eqs. (19), (22), (24), and (26)
entry_problems.result: The one-loop fraternal Higgs potential reproduces v=246 GeV and a 125 GeV Higgs by choosing the quartic and soft symmetry-breaking terms. With cutoff 5 TeV and f approximately 3v, twin-top mass 500–600 GeV, negligible hard breaking rho, and approximately matched twin top/strong/weak couplings, the calculated electroweak tuning is about 20%; the additional tuning of f below the cutoff is negligible in the illustrated weakly coupled scalar regime.

With supersoft breaking, the scalar correction is finite rather than sensitive to a high UV cutoff. The computed negative top/stop contribution cuts its logarithm off at the gaugino mass, typically about five stop masses; roughly 3 TeV stops can satisfy the source-era Higgs bound.

The calculated bachelor benchmark has 1.74 TeV squarks, an 8.25 TeV gluino and negative Higgs soft mass squared of magnitude (500 GeV)^2, with finite supersoft corrections and a stop logarithm cut off by the gluino. The table excludes the mu contribution.

The computed light/heavy-bachelor spectra have 3.45/3.02 TeV squarks and negative Higgs soft scales around 1 TeV/940 GeV. Their finite supersoft corrections and gluino-scale stop cutoff permit the source-era Higgs bound without a large UV logarithm; mu remains a separate input.

For bachelor mass 1e7 GeV and right-handed slepton mass 100 GeV, the threshold-dependent one-loop calculation gives unification near 3e16 GeV with inverse unified coupling 4.5; two-loop and GUT-threshold effects are omitted.

Pre-inflationary KSVZ misalignment has an allowed all-dark-matter region, including the reviewed 0.12 micro-eV to 0.15 meV fit. For the neutral heavy-quark variant, inflation must dilute its stable coloured relics and reheating must avoid regenerating them.

For the neutral colour-triplet KSVZ construction, integrating out the heavy quark generates the required anomaly; the QCD potential minimises effective theta at zero, assuming negligible extra PQ breaking.

The explicit two-singlet charge assignment produces quark textures whose eigenvalue and CKM hierarchies match the source-era observed orders for epsilon1 approximately 0.04 and epsilon2 approximately 0.008. This is an order-of-magnitude quark-flavour result with unspecified order-one coefficients, not a precision fit or prediction of the singlet VEVs.

In the charge-conjugation C branch of the minimal left-right model, the correlated right-handed phases and combined W_R/flavour-changing-Higgs contributions enter the then-preferred B_d and B_s CP-fit regions. The source gives M_WR=2.8 TeV and M_H=15 TeV as a benchmark satisfying its stated bounds while resolving the source-era roughly 2.8-sigma SM discrepancy. The parity P branch does not provide this fit; this is a historical B-physics target.

The gauge-annihilation/coannihilation freeze-out calculation for a Y=0 Majorana weak quintuplet reproduces all of the source-era Omega_DM h^2=0.110+/-0.006 at M=4.4+/-0.1 TeV. This is the paper's leading s-wave, electroweak-symmetric calculation; its quoted mass error is experimental and does not include the acknowledged theoretical uncertainty.

For a Y=0 real scalar weak septuplet with Higgs-portal annihilations assumed negligible, the paper's gauge-annihilation/coannihilation calculation reproduces its observed thermal density at M=8.5+/-0.2 TeV. This uses the leading s-wave, electroweak-symmetric and source-era stability assumptions; the quoted mass error is experimental rather than a complete theoretical error.

For soft breaking retaining supersymmetric dimensionless couplings, the calculated Higgs correction scales as m_soft^2 times a loop factor and log(Lambda_UV/m_soft). With Lambda_UV near the Planck scale, soft masses no larger than roughly TeV protect the weak scale; the stated potential inequalities and minimisation conditions give v=174 GeV. This is conditional technical naturalness.

The displayed general-NMSSM scan contains neutralino points satisfying the paper's experimental constraints and the WMAP relic-density interval, for tan(beta)=5, 0.01<=lambda,kappa<=0.7 and 110 GeV<mu_eff<300 GeV, with the remaining ranges given in Fig. 9. The constrained example also obtains the singlino abundance through stau coannihilation with a mass gap below approximately 8 GeV. These are source-era dark-matter demonstrations reproduced in the review.

locators: Eqs. (26)-(34), especially Eq. (34) and following paragraph
entry_problems.result: Solving the kinetic equations perturbatively gives nB/s approximately 2e-10 delta_CP for a 10 GeV heavier pair with squared-mass splitting ratio near 1e-6; allowed CP factors reproduce the observed roughly 9e-11 while respecting the imposed dark-matter condition.

locators: The nuMSM and dark matter, Eqs. (6)-(9)
entry_problems.result: The demonstrated joint parameter region imposes the observed sterile-neutrino relic-density condition, with M1=2-5 keV, f1 approximately 6e-13 and sufficiently small right-handed mixing angles. The heavier roughly 10 GeV pair also permits the calculated baryon yield without significant entropy dilution.

The constructive normal-spectrum choice sets f2^2=m_sol M2/v^2 and f3^2=m_atm M3/v^2 with m_sol=9.1 meV and m_atm=51 meV; the dark-matter condition leaves the lightest active mass below roughly 1e-5 eV. The active mixing angles remain selectable through the Yukawa rotations.

For a stable, thermalized Z2-odd real singlet, the freeze-out calculation gives mass-portal-coupling curves with the paper's source-era abundance choice Omega_S h^2=0.3, for Higgs masses 100, 120, 140 and 200 GeV. The central cosmological value 0.15 is also obtained by approximately doubling the squared portal coupling. The computed recoil rates leave parameter space allowed by the searches used in the paper. These are historical abundance benchmarks, not a present-day viability claim.

With m_h=125 GeV and a stable real singlet, numerical thermal averaging and Boltzmann evolution produce the Omega_S=Omega_DM contour. The paper overlays the invisible-Higgs, XENON100 and indirect-search constraints, leaving full-abundance solutions near the Higgs resonance and at larger masses. This is the paper's source-era allowed thermal-relic region.

locators: Sec. 2.1, Eq. (2), Dirac fermion plus Higgsed U(1) field inventory
entry_problems.result: For m_psi>m_V, annihilation to two vectors gives the observed thermal abundance when alpha'*(1-m_V^2/m_psi^2)^(1/4) approximately equals 0.005*(m_psi/500 GeV). Small kinetic mixing remains allowed subject to mediator decay before BBN, or the stronger Eq. (15) bound if mixing also maintains thermal equilibrium; the hidden Higgs is chosen heavier than m_V/2.

locators: Sec. 2.2, Eqs. (16)–(18), abundance calculation and direct-search comparison
entry_problems.result: With scalar mediator mass 400 GeV, source-era Higgs mass 120 GeV, and lambda_2 approaching zero, the calculated p-wave annihilation abundance curve fixes beta_h as a function of fermion mass. Its portion above approximately 50 GeV survives the direct-search bound considered in the paper, while collider production is negligible.

For the colour-octet weak-doublet model supplemented by three real Y=0 weak triplets, the paper's one-loop unification calculation using sin^2(theta_W)=0.2312 gives alpha_s(M_Z)=0.122 and M_G=9x10^15 GeV. The source judges this compatible with coupling unification and proton-decay requirements. This result requires the three added triplets and does not apply to the octet-only entry.

For mixed inflation with thermal RH-neutrino production, the analytic leptogenesis conditions admit sufficient asymmetry. The calculation estimates that M near 1e7 GeV with the stated roughly 4% degeneracy enhances the CP source enough while satisfying the stability bound; this is an analytic estimate.

The slow-roll calculation and CMB normalisation yield allowed hidden-scalar/Higgs inflation for nonminimal coupling roughly 1e-3 to 1 and effective quartic roughly 1e-13 to 1e-9; the mixed trajectory also reheats efficiently.

Adding computed vacuum-realignment and estimated string-radiation contributions gives Omega_A h^2 approximately 0.12 for f_A=3e10-1.2e11 GeV, or axion mass 50-200 micro-eV, after PQ restoration; the range includes substantial defect-production uncertainty.
The scan constructs Yukawas from measured PMNS mixing and two measured neutrino masses, setting the lightest mass to zero; normal and inverted spectra are both implemented through the type-I seesaw.
The down-type quark supplies the PQ colour anomaly; the calculated axion potential has its absolute minimum at A/f_A=0, dynamically removing effective strong theta.

The explicit stable 45H+126H spectrum with a (6,3,1/3) threshold at 5.57e11 GeV and B-L VEV 1.46e14 GeV yields one-loop gauge unification compatible with the paper's Super-Kamiokande bound. This result concerns the calculated Higgs sector, without a fermion fit.

Including neutralino/chargino coannihilation, the computed thermal density meets the WMAP interval for a predominantly Higgsino LSP of 1.0-1.2 TeV or a predominantly wino LSP of 2.0-2.5 TeV; these are source-era relic calculations.

Two-loop running with separate one-loop gluino, electroweakino and scalar thresholds gives unification predictions compatible with the measured strong coupling for heavy scalar scales, using mu=M2, M2=300 GeV or 1 TeV and unified gaugino masses. Unknown GUT thresholds prevent firm parameter bounds.

locators: Sec. III, Tables I-III and final threshold scenarios
entry_problems.result: A one-loop threshold solution has a roughly 1.5 TeV fermion triplet and unification near 3e16 GeV, with Phi1 and Sigma8 near the electroweak scale and Sigma3 and Phi3 at the GUT scale; proton-decay conditions are discussed separately.

locators: Sec. II, Eqs. (5)-(7) and following normal/inverted spectra
entry_problems.result: The calculated rank-two type-I+III mass matrix admits one massless neutrino and two eigenvalues explicitly fixed by the measured solar and atmospheric splittings, for either ordering; the two independent Yukawa vectors allow these spectra.

locators: Eqs. (1)–(3) and the following discussion of two complete SM copies: twin symmetry makes quadratic mass corrections SU(4)-invariant
final two body paragraphs before the summary, beginning 'Let us now turn to mirror symmetric models (and twin symmetric models without the extended top sector)'
entry_problems.result: For the unextended twin spectrum, in the heavy radial-mode limit, the paper calculates weak-scale stabilization with f=800 GeV and cutoff about 10 TeV at approximately 11% tuning, or f=500 GeV and cutoff about 6 TeV at approximately 31% tuning. The corresponding source-era Higgs masses are 166 and 153 GeV. These are specifically the benchmarks without the extra top-sector quarks.

locators: Sec. III, Eq. (18), Proca EFT with vector self-coupling set to zero
entry_problems.result: The thermal-relic calculation finds an allowed WMAP abundance band in (m_X,lambda_hv), including the Higgs resonance for m_h=150 GeV, that survives source-era XENON100 bounds. The three-parameter scan also retains points after ATLAS/CMS constraints. This is the Z2 Proca EFT calculation; its retained weak-coupling band obeys the paper's unitarity requirement.

For a single (B,Y) vector-like doublet mixing predominantly with the third generation, the LEP-era Z-pole fit using the paper's second SM prediction set has sin(theta_R)=0.157 and improves chi^2 from 10.97 (four degrees of freedom) to 1.61 (three). The preferred mixing is compatible with the paper's oblique bounds for m_B<=1.9 TeV, or m_B approximately <=1.1 TeV if the off-diagonal Yukawa is limited to the SM top Yukawa. This addresses the historical A_FB^b discrepancy.
